Liam Chen: hi team! quick onboarding puzzles before my start on Tue. 1) I'm transitioning from contractor to FT mid-month — does medical/dental start immediately on my official start date or the 1st of next month? 2) I had to pick up a prescription while traveling for relocation (receipts in my name, paid with my UK card). Can I submit that for reimbursement under medical? If so, where do I upload and do you need an itemized pharmacy receipt vs a credit card slip? 3) I tried to finish the I-9 but the verification office is closed for the observed holiday on Monday — will that block payroll setup?

Noah (People Ops): welcome Liam! :wave: Short answers: (1) Benefits effective date is your official FT start date per offer unless HR flagged otherwise. We still need to confirm plan enrollment windows with Benefits vendor, but typically coverage is effective that day. (2) Prescription: yes you can submit as a medical reimbursement. We need an itemized pharmacy receipt showing drug name, date, amount, and pharmacy name. Card slip alone isn't sufficient. Upload to our benefits portal (link: https://benefits.redwood.com/claims) and tag "newhire-med" so we expedite. If foreign currency, include exchange info (currency and conversion date).

Noah (People Ops): (3) I-9: if in-person ID verification can't happen before payroll cutoff because of the holiday, Payroll will onboard you but put tax status in pending until the I-9 is complete. Please book an I-9 verification slot first thing Tue. If you cannot verify in person, we have an alternate remote doc verification flow for international hires. (DM me if needed).

Jasmin (Payroll): note on payroll setup: Taxes and benefits enrollment feed from Workday into payroll nightly. If I-9 is late, you may still be paid but some withholdings (like pre-tax commuter or certain voluntary deductions) might be delayed until enrollment completes. Reimbursements (medical/relocation) are separate AP processes. For the prescription claim, if we pay via reimbursement it will appear on the next AP run (usually within 7 business days after approval).

Liam Chen: thanks both. quick follow-ups: for the RX I paid GBP 24.50 on 2026-04-12 while in Heathrow. Should I attach bank statement snippet showing the charge or is the pharmacy receipt enough? Also, who signs off medical claims for newhires (manager vs benefits team)?

Noah (People Ops): attach both if it's easy — pharmacy receipt + bank statement snippet helps with verification for foreign charges. Sign-off: benefits team does the final approval, but we sometimes need manager confirmation if it's a policy edge-case. For standard prescriptions it's just benefits.
